Answer: A
Reason: Intralobar pulmonary sequestration typically presents as a well-defined, homogeneous mass in the lower lobes (often near the diaphragm), which corresponds to the sequestered lung tissue supplied by systemic arteries (as highlighted by the arrows in the 3D reconstruction). The other options describe findings more consistent with heart failure, infection, or emphysema rather than a congenital sequestration.
